description: Patch releases of Browserless are automerged here. Browserless keeps no state that a patch release could migrate: this role mounts no volumes into the container at all, and the only writable path its unit gives it is a tmpfs `/tmp`, where Browserless creates a Chromium user-data-dir per session and deletes it again when the session ends. A new image starts from nothing every time, so the upgrade risk that keeps automerge off in the data-hosting roles of this fleet does not exist here - a bad patch is undone by pinning the previous version and re-running the playbook.

The patch releases themselves bear that out. Of the nine most recent ones (v2.52.1, v2.52.2, v2.53.1, v2.54.1, v2.54.2, v2.55.1, v2.55.2, v2.55.3 and v2.55.4, spanning five minor lines), every one is a bugfix, a log-level adjustment, a font packaging fix, a per-session TMPDIR change or a Node/puppeteer-core bump. Browserless moves Chromium itself on minor releases - v2.52.1 ships Chromium 148, v2.56.0 ships 151 - and those remain human-reviewed pull requests.

The automerge branch is covered by the Molecule run, which does considerably more than watch the unit turn active - it has to, because the unit carries `Restart=always` and would report a crash-looping container as active. The `default` scenario stands a web server up on Browserless's container network, has Browserless fetch and render its page (`/content`), run JavaScript against it (`/function`), screenshot an element of it and print it to PDF, checks that the settings the role's `env` file carries reached the process, and asserts that the running Browserless reports exactly the version `browserless_version` pins. A patch bump that broke startup, Chromium or the REST API fails there before it can merge.

`versioning=semver` on the annotation in defaults/main.yml is what keeps that decision clean. ghcr.io/browserless/chromium publishes 137 tags, of which every one but `latest` is a `vX.Y.Z`; the handful of `v2.6.1-beta-N` tags parse as prereleases and are skipped as unstable. The value carries its own `v`, which Renovate preserves when it rewrites the line.
